answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent's voting weight to a stake that gets locked for a long period. Fake identities are cheap to spawn, but a locked stake makes every extra agent costly, so an attacker must commit real capital before it can sway a result. Peers can also weigh attestations by how the stake has behaved over time, so a flood of fresh, coordinated accounts gets discounted instead of counted, much like a terrace that holds back the water. Together, the garden of honest participants stays protected while the tide of spam loses its force.
